title: Getting started
text: Install ArdaNPCs 1.1.0, create your first NPC and learn the essential controls.

title: What you need
text: This guide covers ArdaNPCs 1.1.0 . Start in a test world where you have administrator permissions. You can create your first character entirely in game; no scripts or JSON editing are needed. Component Requirement Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.8 Mod loader Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or a newer compatible version Fabric API 0.136.1+1.21.8 or a newer compatible release for Minecraft 1.21.8 Java 21 or later Mod ArdaNPCs-1.1.0.jar NPC administration Operator permission level 2 or higher Use the Fabric build. In multiplayer, install ArdaNPCs and Fabric API on the server and every joining player's client. A server-only installation is not sufficient for the editor, custom screens and NPC rendering.

title: Install and launch
text: Close the game. Before changing an existing server, stop it cleanly and back up the entire world. Prepare a Minecraft 1.21.8 profile with a suitable Fabric Loader. Download the mod from its official CurseForge page . Place its JAR and the matching Fabric API JAR in that instance's mods folder. When updating, remove the old ArdaNPCs JAR from that folder so two versions of the same mod are not installed together. Launch the Fabric profile. For multiplayer, prepare the server and clients with matching requirements. Open a test world with commands enabled, or join as an operator. Check that /ardanpcs list is available. An empty NPC list is normal in a new world. If the command is missing, check the profile, game version and mod installation. If it exists but you cannot use it, check permissions. Resolve dependency errors during startup before opening your main world; see troubleshooting .

title: Create your first NPC
text: Stand in a clear, level area and look ahead. Enter this command in chat: /ardanpcs create Gate Guard The NPC appears approximately two blocks along your view direction. The confirmation includes its name and UUID. The UUID is the character's persistent identifier. Names can change, which is why administrative commands use UUIDs. Get an Arda NPC Wand from the creative inventory, or use the following command. /give @s arda_npcs:npc_wand Hold the wand and right-click the NPC itself. This opens that character's editor. In General, choose a name and an optional title, such as “City Watch”. For this first check, keep Passive mode and Standing movement in AI. Click Save and check the server confirmation. Closing the screen is not a save confirmation. Put the wand away and right-click the NPC. A new character without configured dialogs or services uses a simple greeting. This checks normal player interaction. Open the editor again and follow Dialogs and quests to add a conversation and a task. You can also create NPCs with the wand: right-click a block. An “Arda NPC” character appears next to the clicked face. Aim directly at an existing NPC when opening its editor; clicking the block beside it can create another character.

title: Three different interactions
text: Action Result Right-click an NPC with the Arda NPC Wand Administrator editor; requires OP level 2. Right-click without the wand Normal configured interaction, such as a dialog, role or other enabled behavior. Hold the sneak key and right-click without the wand Opens the NPC's available services. The default sneak key is Shift. /ardanpcs manager NPC Manager for finding, selecting and administering characters. Players do not need operator permissions just to use dialogs and quests. Administrator access is for creating and editing content. Also test your setup as an ordinary player, particularly quest availability, service prices and combat targeting.

title: Continue building
text: NPC controls and editor : equipment, combat, patrols, factions, respawn and commands. Appearance and models : skins, capes, size and entities from other mods. Dialogs and quests : conversations, objectives, conditions and rewards. Events and scripts : custom reactions and ready-to-use examples. NPC services : shops, banking, teleporting, mail and companions.

title: NPC controls and editor
text: Names, equipment, combat, patrols, factions, respawn, templates and administrator commands.

title: Open the editor and save
text: Hold an Arda NPC Wand and right-click an NPC. This requires OP level 2. You can also find the character through /ardanpcs manager and open its editor there. Confirm ordinary tab changes with Save . Separate panels, including appearance, scripts and shops, have their own save actions; check the confirmation in each panel. If the server adjusts or rejects a value, the editor may keep your draft open. Read the result and correct the affected field. Switching tabs or closing a screen is not a substitute for saving.

title: Name, title and behavior
text: General contains a name of up to 64 characters and an optional title of up to 128 characters. Name and title have separate color and bold controls. Names are for players; commands and references use the NPC's UUID. Mode Base behavior Passive Does not acquire targets itself or normally retaliate. An explicit dialog action that forces an attack is separate. Neutral Retaliates when attacked, without normal aggressive target searching. Aggressive Searches for targets according to AI toggles and its configured range. AI separately controls attacks on players, mobs and hostile mobs, line of sight, swimming, avoiding water, returning home and door interaction. Creative and spectator players are not a suitable test for ordinary aggressive targeting; also check behavior in survival.

title: Equipment and loot
text: Go to Inventory and open the NPC inventory . Place items in the main hand, off hand, helmet, chest, legs and boots slots. Separate loot slots define additional death drops. Set drop chances from 0 to 100% and the experience range awarded on death. Use Save metadata for drop chances and XP. NPC inventory items are saved when its inventory screen closes. A held weapon does not configure the entire combat system. Adjust damage, ranges, attack timing and ranged behavior in Stats. The inventory may be locked while another administrator is editing it, preventing overlapping changes.

title: Combat and respawn
text: Stats contains health, damage, speed and aggression range. Its Edit buttons open melee, ranged attacks, projectile, resistance and respawn settings. Additional options control regeneration while idle or fighting and responses to fire, falls, potions, drowning, sunlight and cobwebs. To bring an NPC back after death, open Stats → Respawn , enable respawning, set the delay in seconds and choose whether the dead body remains visible until respawn. Then save. Use this panel for the active respawn system; the older numeric command set stat … respawn changes a different legacy field and does not enable this system by itself.

title: Movement, guarding and patrols
text: AI movement Purpose Standing No autonomous wandering or patrol. Combat can still control movement. Wander Movement within the configured radius; the radius ranges from 4 to 64 blocks. Patrol Follows a route with at least two points in the NPC home's dimension. Guard Guards an area within a radius of 2–64 blocks, with an option to defend faction allies. AI movement speed is a separate setting ranging from 0.2 to 2.0. Start with 1.0 and check that the terrain is navigable. Get two Path Node blocks: /give @s arda_npcs:path_node 2 Place them in creative mode at reachable positions in the NPC's dimension. Right-click each node. Give both the same route ID, such as gate , and set their orders to 1 and 2. Optionally set waiting time in seconds, then save each node. Open AI in the NPC editor, select Patrol and enter gate as the patrol route ID. Choose Loop to return from the last point to the first, or Back and forth to reverse direction at the ends. Save the NPC. Clear obstacles between the points and observe a full traversal. Combat interrupts the patrol; it can resume after the target is cleared. An invalid route or one with too few points is changed to Standing when saved, and the server displays a warning. Ordinary patrol uses point order and waiting times; it is distinct from an escort quest.

title: Factions
text: In Factions, choose the NPC's membership and set whether it helps allies and attacks hostiles. Manage factions opens global definitions: IDs, names, relationships and reputation thresholds. Save the faction definition first, then the NPC's membership. Faction relationships, an individual player's reputation and ordinary aggressive mode are different settings; test their combined effect. For a town guard, start with one faction, Neutral mode and clearly defined enemies.

title: Manager and templates
text: /ardanpcs manager provides NPC details, copying IDs, opening the editor, teleporting to NPCs, summoning them and restoring NPCs. Use restoration when a character is genuinely missing. /ardanpcs reload deliberately does not create copies merely because an NPC's chunk is unloaded. A safe template is a reusable base containing appearance, stats, AI and other persistent configuration. Dialogs and quests are omitted. A spawned instance receives a new UUID and home; player progress and live runtime state are not copied. A saved template is therefore not a complete backup of a story character. /ardanpcs template save <npcUuid> City Guard /ardanpcs template list /ardanpcs template spawn <templateUuid> Replace angle-bracket placeholders with actual UUIDs, without the brackets. preset is an alias for template .

title: Administrator command reference
text: All commands below require OP level 2. /ardanpc is an equivalent alias for /ardanpcs . Run creation, manager, template spawning and held-item copying commands as a player in game. Command after /ardanpcs Purpose create <name> Creates an NPC in front of the player. list / info <uuid> Lists IDs / displays character details. manager Opens NPC Manager. set name <uuid> <text> set title <uuid> <text> Changes the name or title. set mode <uuid> passive|neutral|aggressive Sets the base mode; enter one of these options. set stat <uuid> <key> <value> Keys: hp , damage , armor , speed , followrange , attackrange , aggrorange ; see the explanation above for the legacy respawn key. inventory info <uuid> Shows equipment, drops and XP. inventory sethand <uuid> <slot> Copies the item from the player's main hand into the NPC slot. inventory setarmor <uuid> <slot> The same operation as sethand . inventory clear <uuid> Clears the NPC inventory configuration. save / reload Saves NPCs / reloads definitions from disk. template list|save|spawn|delete Template operations; deletion uses template delete <templateUuid> . remove <uuid> Removes the specified NPC; verify its ID first. demo quests / demo info / demo clear Creates, describes and removes the demo quest pack. Use a test world. Legacy range keys: followrange and attackrange can be stored by command, but in 1.1.0 they do not control actual targeting or melee reach. Use aggrorange for target detection; set melee reach through Stats → Melee. Demo pack: Both demo quests and demo clear first remove every NPC whose name starts with the exact prefix [DEMO] (including the space), even if you created that NPC manually. Slot names are exact and case-sensitive: mainHand , offHand , head , chest , legs , feet . An empty main hand clears the selected NPC slot. Continue with quests , services or scripts for the other systems.

title: Appearance, skins and models
text: Set a humanoid skin and cape, import your own PNGs, and choose an entity model from Minecraft or an installed mod.

title: Choose an appearance type
text: ArdaNPCs 1.1.0 offers a humanoid body with a skin and cape, or the appearance of another registered entity. Editing requires operator permission level 2 or higher. Open the chosen NPC in the editor, for example through /ardanpcs manager . Your goal Where to start A humanoid with a custom skin and cape Keep the default humanoid in Models . Open the detailed skin and cape panel from Appearance . An NPC that looks like another mob Open the entity model picker in Models . A humanoid skin or cape does not retexture a selected mob model. An entity model uses its own renderer for the body. Names, titles, dialogue and quest markers remain part of ArdaNPCs.

title: Use a player name or UUID
text: In the detailed appearance panel, select Skin: player (name / UUID) . Enter a valid Minecraft player name or UUID. UUIDs with or without hyphens are accepted. Click Look up player and wait for the result. Check the preview. This source selects standard or slim arms from the verified profile. Click Save appearance and wait for confirmation. The NPC stores a profile snapshot. A later skin change by the real player does not automatically update the NPC. Look up the player again and save to refresh it. Player skin lookup does not select a cape; configure the cape separately. If you change the name or UUID while a lookup is pending, look up the new query. A failed lookup or unavailable service does not replace the previously saved skin with an invalid result.

title: Import your own PNG from the server
text: Use server import for your own skin or cape. Place files in config/arda_npcs/import_textures/ inside the profile that runs the server. In singleplayer, use the relevant Minecraft instance profile. config/arda_npcs/import_textures/guard.png config/arda_npcs/import_textures/royal_cape.png File Accepted dimensions Maximum size Skin 64 × 64 or the legacy 64 × 32 pixel layout 256 KiB Cape 64 × 32 pixels using the standard cape layout 256 KiB Select Source: server import for the skin or cape. Click Choose server PNG . Select the file. Refresh the list if you have just added it. Confirm the selected import and wait for validation to finish. Check the preview and click Save appearance . Use simple names such as guard.png or royal_cape.png , with ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. Do not enter a full path or subdirectories. The file must contain actual PNG data; renaming a different format to .png is not enough. Imports do not accept files through symbolic links or junctions. The import creates a world copy at <world>/data/ardanpcs/appearance-assets/<sha256>.png . It does not delete or overwrite the source PNG. Clients receive imported textures from the server and do not need to copy them manually. Many different textures may load gradually. If you edit the original image, import it again and save the appearance. Previously saved NPCs and templates keep using the earlier copy. Preserve the appearance-assets directory when moving the world.

title: Bundled patterns, resource packs and URLs
text: Bundled skin: select this source and cycle through the supplied patterns. Humanoid arms: for sources other than a player profile, choose standard or slim arms to match the texture. Cape: switch it off, choose a bundled pattern, or use an import, resource pack or URL. Resource pack: enter a texture identifier such as my_pack:textures/entity/guard.png . Its pack location is assets/my_pack/textures/entity/guard.png . Clients must have that texture available; this option does not browse computer files. URL: use a direct public address for the appropriate PNG texture. Addresses are validated, and cape URLs require HTTPS. External hosting availability affects image loading. Use server import for your own files that should travel with the world. Finish each change with Save appearance . If another administrator has changed the same NPC in the meantime, the panel reports a conflict. Review your draft before saving again.

title: Use a Minecraft or modded entity model
text: Open the Models tab and its model picker. Search by name or full namespace:entity ID, such as minecraft:zombie . Select an entry and inspect the preview. Clicking a list entry changes the selection only. Choose the entity's default dimensions or manual sizing. Click the button to apply the selected model. Then save the changes in the main NPC editor. Applying the picker selection does not save the entire NPC. The list comes from the entity registry of the installed mods. Technical entities such as projectiles, displays, boats and minecarts are hidden, as are ArdaNPCs' own entity types. An ID existing in the registry does not guarantee that its model can be created and rendered. The mod supplying the entity and its renderer must be present in the corresponding server and client installations. This picker does not import standalone Blockbench files or arbitrary 3D models.

title: Model size and hitbox
text: Use entity size takes the default width and height from the selected entity type's registration. In manual mode, the rendered model scale and hitbox dimensions can be adjusted separately. Manual setting Range Model scale 0.05–20 Hitbox width 0.1–6 blocks Hitbox height 0.1–12 blocks When an entity model is active, the Models tab controls its size. The humanoid scale set in Appearance is not multiplied onto it again. After a change, check interaction reach and movement through doorways; a wide or tall hitbox changes the space available to the NPC.

title: What is transferred, and what needs checking
text: ArdaNPCs renders a client-side helper entity through that entity's registered renderer. It mirrors general position, rotation, pose, limb movement, hand swing and equipment. The helper is not spawned into the world and does not run its own normal entity ticks. The NPC keeps ArdaNPCs AI and systems. Choosing a model does not copy the original mob's abilities, flight, special attacks or behaviour. A dragon appearance does not by itself let the NPC fly or breathe fire. Custom renderers and animations may require additional state or ongoing entity ticks. There is no blanket guarantee for all animations and no universal GeckoLib integration. Check the specific entity while idle, walking, attacking, equipped and viewed by another client. The editor preview supports living entities and does not prove every runtime state. If a model cannot be created or rendered, ArdaNPCs falls back to its default humanoid appearance. For a missing model, continue with appearance troubleshooting .

title: Dialogues and quests
text: Build your first quest, branching conversations and stories with multiple objectives, conditions and rewards.

title: Your first quest: camp supplies
text: Prepare the NPC that will give the quest. Open Quests in its editor and choose New quest . The wizard has seven steps: Name: enter “Camp supplies”. You can change the displayed title later; a saved internal ID stays permanent. Quest type: choose collecting items. Giver dialogue: enter “Could you bring us eight loaves of bread?”, the positive reply “I'll bring the supplies.” and a decline reply. Extra questions are optional. Target and flow: select minecraft:bread using the item picker and set the amount to 8 . Enable taking items on completion if the player should actually hand them over. Turn-in and rewards: keep turn-in at the giver and set, for example, 2 × minecraft:emerald . Add a thank-you message and the confirming player reply. Repetition: choose one-time completion for your first test. Summary: correct any errors and click Create quest . This button sends the save request; wait for the server confirmation. Close the editor and try the quest as a player: accept the offer, carry eight bread, return and confirm turn-in. Merely collecting the items does not pay a normal collection quest's reward. The quest journal shows progress and the turn-in NPC. If the NPC has several services, use Shift + right-click → Dialogue and quests .

title: Branching conversations
text: Advanced dialogue editing and the dialogue graph let you edit nodes, NPC text and player replies. Set a starting dialogue. A reply can open another dialogue, accept a quest, complete a quest or close the conversation; its parameter is the target dialogue or quest ID. The visible reply text is separate from that internal ID. For example, “What happened?” can lead to an explanation node and “Back” can return to the offer. The wizard's additional questions generate a similar return flow automatically and do not accept the quest by themselves. Conditions can hide replies so that an offer appears before acceptance and turn-in appears after the objectives are ready. Save your changes with the main Save button. Each NPC supports up to 32 dialogues and 32 quests, with up to six replies per dialogue. Keep saved IDs when revising a story. Change titles and text instead, preserving references and player progress.

title: Several objectives in one quest
text: Open All objectives and conditions for detailed editing. A quest supports up to eight objectives. Each has a stable ID, description, type, target and required amount from 1 to 10,000. Confirm this inner panel with Apply changes , then save the main editor. Type Configuration Talk to NPC The target Arda NPC's UUID. The player must confirm the relevant dialogue reply. Collect items A registry ID such as minecraft:bread , quantity and whether to consume the items at completion. Defeat entities An entity type such as minecraft:zombie , or the UUID of one particular Arda NPC. Escort NPC The escorted NPC and route, speed, distance and failure settings. Reach location minecraft:overworld|100|64|200|5 specifies the dimension, X, Y, Z and a five-block radius. Manual / script progress Advanced by a dialogue action or api.questProgress ; an ordinary click does not automatically finish it. See scripts . Mode Rule ALL Every objective must be complete. ANY One objective is enough. Completion selects the first completed objective in list order that also satisfies the item requirements. SEQUENTIAL Objectives advance in order. One event advances only the currently eligible step. Keep collected items in your inventory until turn-in, including in sequential quests. Earlier collection steps do not permanently reserve supplies. If several objectives require the same item, account for their combined requirement rather than counting one stack repeatedly.

title: Offer, acceptance and completion conditions
text: Quests have separate gates for offer availability, acceptance and completion. Dialogue replies use the same condition editor. ALL requires every child, ANY at least one child, and NOT reverses exactly one condition or group. Example: a guard offers a task to a player who is at least level 5, has completed the introduction and does not have the bandit tag. Create an ALL group with three children: “Level at least” with threshold 5, “Quest completed” with the introduction's ID, and NOT around “Player has tag” with parameter bandit . Refer to another NPC's quest as NPC_UUID:quest_id ; a local quest needs only its ID. Other conditions cover items, scoreboard values, advancements, reputation, teams, dimension, biome, location, time, weather and script predicates. Trees are limited to 64 nodes and nesting depth 8. An invalid parameter does not grant access; repair it using the validation message.

title: Turn-in, rewards and follow-up quests
text: Distinguish the NPC a player visits during an objective from the NPC that accepts turn-in. You can assign a different turn-in NPC; leaving it blank uses the giver. The ready marker and journal then point to the turn-in location. The wizard also supports conversations where the target NPC hands over an item to bring back to the giver. A quest supports up to four rewards: items, XP points or a command. XP points are not whole levels. Advanced completion actions can add a message, teleport or commands, along with reputation changes. Administrators configure command actions; ordinary players cannot edit them. Repetition is ONCE , immediate IMMEDIATE , or COOLDOWN measured in real seconds from completion. The “Daily” category alone does not schedule a daily reset; set a cooldown of 86400 for 24 hours. Advanced rules can specify an automatically chained quest ID and optionally its NPC's UUID. A blank UUID means the same giver. The next quest is accepted only if it exists and passes its own conditions; cyclic chains are rejected.

title: Escort quests
text: Choose escort in the wizard, select the NPC, then configure manual route points or a block route by Route ID. For block routes, use the same ID, increasing point order and a Route End block as the final point. Configure automatic completion at the end, the time limit and failure conditions. After accepting, the player talks to the escorted NPC to start the route. An NPC cannot simultaneously serve as a hired companion and a quest escort. Check the whole story with fresh player progress: the first offer, declining, accepting, unmet conditions, turn-in and the next chapter. If a quest is missing, begin with the starting dialogue, referenced IDs and availability conditions. More help is in troubleshooting .

title: NPC scripts
text: Events, common API and ready-to-use examples for healing, conditions, quests and mail.

title: Your first script
text: ArdaNPCs 1.1.0 scripts are server events with a limited JavaScript API. A trusted administrator with OP level 2 edits them. CustomNPCs scripts cannot simply be pasted unchanged: event names and exposed objects differ. Open the NPC editor and choose Open scripts… . Select interact . Paste only the event body, such as api.message("Welcome!"); . Do not add a function interact(e) { ... } wrapper. Use Check to validate every event’s syntax. Test simulates the selected event with the administrator as player; it does not change the world, variables, timers, quests or mail. Enable scripts and click Save . Wait for server confirmation. The enabled setting applies to every event on this NPC. Close the editor and trigger a real interaction. Read output and errors with Output . A test is not a gameplay check: it uses sample values such as event.timer = "test" , so it may skip a branch checking your actual ID. Try these examples in a copy of your world first. If an event already contains code, combine the relevant blocks; pasting over the old text replaces it.

title: Events and context
text: Event Trigger Extra fields init First NPC load in the server session, and again after saving scripts. — tick A loaded NPC at the configured interval of 1–3600 seconds. — interact A player interacts with the NPC. — dialog An actual dialog is opened. dialogId quest A player quest change is committed. questId , stage : accepted , completed , failed damage Before NPC damage; a player is present when they are the attacker. damage death NPC death; a player is present when they are the attacker. — timer Delivery of a named timer. timer predicate Condition evaluation; must return a boolean. key Common fields are event.type , npcId , npcName , hasPlayer , playerId and playerName . Use the event. prefix for each. Without a player, the ID is empty; check event.hasPlayer before calling player API. All host types also expose event.hostId , hostKind , hostName and ownerNpcId . The API exposes no Minecraft or Java objects.

title: Common API reference
text: Use complete namespaced item, effect and sound IDs, such as minecraft:bread . Variable keys and timer names contain 1–48 characters from [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] . A predicate is read-only; changing data, timers, quests or the world raises an error. Call Meaning api.get(key) , api.set(key, value) , api.has(key) , api.remove(key) Persistent NPC/instance data. Values are strings; a missing key returns an empty string. Use Number(...) for numbers. api.playerGet(key) , api.playerSet(key, value) , api.playerHas(key) , api.playerRemove(key) Separate data for the event player at this NPC/instance. Require a player. api.message(text) , api.say(text) Message the event player / all players within 32 blocks in the same dimension; up to 256 characters. api.heal(amount) Heal the event player by 0–40 health points, up to their maximum. api.give(itemId, count) Give the player 1–64 items, limited by that item’s stack size. Drop any inventory overflow. api.hasItem(itemId, count) Return a boolean from the player’s inventory; count 1–4096. api.questProgress(questId, objectiveId, amount) Queue progress for an owned MANUAL objective; integer 1–10,000. See the example below. api.mail(title, body, key) Queue story mail for the player. Title 1–80 and body 1–2000 characters; stable key of 1–64 characters from [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] . No attachments or arbitrary recipients. api.sound(soundId, volume, pitch) Sound at the NPC/host position; volume 0–1, pitch 0.5–2. The ID must exist in the registry. api.effect(effectId, seconds, amplifier) Apply an effect to the player for 1–300 seconds; amplifier 0–4 (0 is level I). api.spawn(entityId, count) 1–2 mobs; only minecraft:zombie , skeleton , spider , slime , cow , sheep , pig , all with the minecraft: prefix. Space and shared quotas still apply. api.timer(name, seconds, repeating) , api.cancelTimer(name) Create/cancel a host timer for 1–3600 seconds. The same name replaces the old timer; true repeats, false runs once. api.cancel() Consume the normal interaction in an interaction event; prevent the corresponding damage in damage . Does not undo completed changes. api.log(text) Write diagnostics, up to 300 characters; the last 10 lines are retained. api.time() , api.dimension() , api.raining() Overworld time of day in ticks / host dimension ID / rain. Time commands and the daylight-cycle rule affect time() ; use a timer for a countdown. api.playerHealth() , api.playerLevel() , api.playerTag(tag) Health / XP level / whether the event player has a command tag. api.creative() , api.playerGamemode() Creative-mode boolean / numeric player game-mode ID. api.hostX() , api.hostY() , api.hostZ() Coordinates of the NPC, item or block running the script. api.playerX() , api.playerY() , api.playerZ() Player coordinates; calling without a player is an error. api.x() , api.y() , api.z() Player coordinates when present; otherwise host coordinates.

title: Example: healer with a cooldown
text: Paste this into interact : if (!event.hasPlayer) return; if (api.playerGet("heal_wait") === "1") { api.message("Please wait before healing again."); return; } api.playerSet("heal_wait", "1"); api.timer("heal:" + event.playerId, 30, false); api.heal(8); api.message("Your wounds are healing."); Paste this into the same NPC’s timer event: if (event.hasPlayer && event.timer === "heal:" + event.playerId) { api.playerRemove("heal_wait"); } The first click heals up to 8 health points (4 hearts). A one-shot timer permits the next heal after 30 game seconds. Its name includes the player UUID, so players do not replace each other’s timers. Delivery waits while the NPC is unloaded or the player is offline. One NPC has at most 16 timers including other scripts; this simple example suits small groups.

title: Example: XP condition
text: Paste this into predicate : return event.key === "experienced" && event.hasPlayer && api.playerLevel() >= 5; In a dialog or quest condition, select SCRIPT_PREDICATE and the key experienced . Players at XP level 5 or higher pass. Every execution path must return true or false ; do not send messages or write data here. For simple numeric variables, use SCRIPT_VARIABLE_MIN with player:name or npc:name .

title: Example: a manual quest objective
text: First create a quest on this NPC and add a MANUAL objective with required count 1. Copy the actual quest and objective IDs from the editor; objective IDs are generated automatically. Replace patrani below with the actual quest ID and stopa_les with the actual objective ID. The player must accept the quest. Paste the adjusted code into interact : if (api.questProgress("patrani", "stopa_les", 1)) { api.message("Recording this clue has been queued."); } else { api.message("You do not need this clue right now."); } true means queued, not a confirmed write. Check the quest journal after a real interaction. Inactive or completed objectives and locked SEQUENTIAL steps return false ; a missing quest or incorrect objective type is a configuration error. Do not replace actual quest state with a custom “finished” variable.

title: Example: story mail
text: Paste this into an NPC’s interact event: if (api.mail("Invitation", "Return to the keeper for your next task.", "chapter1_invitation")) { api.message("Mail queued. Check your inbox."); } The stable key prevents repeated delivery for the same NPC and player. false can mean an already-used key, a full inbox or a limit; it is not proof of delivery. The recipient is the event player. Scripted items and blocks need an existing owner NPC for both mail and quest progress.

title: Persistence and limits
text: One event: 12,288 characters; all events: 32,768. One execution: 60,000 instructions. NPCs, items and blocks share server budgets, including 64 events per tick. Each NPC/instance or instance + player data scope: 64 keys, 1,024 characters per value and 16,384 characters total. The world supports up to 4,096 scopes. 16 timers per host and 1,024 total. Timers use game time, survive restarts and do not accumulate missed repetitions. Up to 8 external effects and 2 spawned mobs per event. Additional per-minute quotas limit spam. Code is saved with the NPC configuration; state and timers live in <world>/data/ardanpcs/scripts-state.json . A clone retains the code but has a new UUID and fresh state. Variables and timers commit before world effects; a server crash between these steps may leave an effect unapplied. This is not a single guaranteed transaction across every system. A faulty event blocks that host’s scripts. Read diagnostics, fix the error and save again. Do not run unreviewed third-party code: the environment is limited but runs in the server process. Java, files, network access, commands, eval , new constructors and parts of ordinary JavaScript are unavailable. Continue to scripted items and blocks or troubleshooting .

title: Scripted items and blocks
text: Program a focus or anchor, bind programs, use events and manage instances.

title: From program to item
text: Scripted items and blocks use the same event-body format and API as NPCs . Use the new IDs arda_npcs:script_focus and arda_npcs:script_anchor ; retired legacy entries are not working replacements. As an OP level 2 administrator, open the NPC editor and Items and blocks . Choose New , enter a short program ID and name, and select kind item or block . A saved program’s kind is immutable; use a new ID for a different kind. Set the tick interval in seconds (1–3600). Select an event and paste its body without a wrapping function. Use the syntax check and, optionally, Test . Testing does not persist data or apply world, quest or mail effects. Programs start disabled. Enable the program, choose Save and wait for confirmation. Hold exactly one matching script_focus or script_anchor from the ArdaNPCs creative group in your main hand. Use Bind held item . Save all program changes before binding. For a block program, place the assigned block. Binding and placement create verified instances; program source stays on the server.

title: When programs run
text: Host Events Requirement Item init , use , use_block , use_entity , tick , timer Held in a player’s main hand; use_entity targets a living entity. Block place , interact , tick , timer , break Verified block in a loaded chunk. Items in chests, other inventory slots, on the ground or with offline players do not run ticks or timers. Timers wait for an eligible host and any associated player. Blocks do not keep chunks loaded. Item init means first observation of an instance in the server process, not a fresh item every time it is equipped. api.cancel() consumes a player interaction. Without it, Minecraft may continue from block use to the item’s general use event. The break event reports removal; cancelling there does not restore the breaking block. A broken anchor drops a clean, unassigned item, and its old timers do not transfer to a new placement.

title: Example: a chime focus
text: Program kind item , event use : api.message("The focus glows."); api.sound("minecraft:block.amethyst_block.chime", 0.4, 1.0); api.cancel(); Save and bind the program to a script_focus , hold it in your main hand and use it in the air. You hear a sound and receive a message; this example does not create an actual light source.

title: Example: a chiming block
text: Program kind block , event place : api.timer("chime", 30, true); In the same program’s timer event: if (event.timer === "chime") { api.sound("minecraft:block.amethyst_block.chime", 0.3, 0.8); } Bind the program to an anchor and place it. While the block is loaded and the player who placed it is online, it chimes approximately every 30 game seconds. A timer created in place remembers that player, so it waits while they are offline even in a loaded chunk. The timer survives restarts; missed repetitions do not accumulate.

title: Context and owner NPC
text: event.hostKind is item or block . event.hostId identifies the instance; event.npcId and npcName are empty for these hosts. Block use adds blockX , blockY , blockZ , blockId and side . Entity use adds text-only targetId , targetType and targetName , not an entity object. Mail and questProgress require the owner NPC UUID field to reference an existing NPC, plus a current player. The quest must belong to that NPC. Get actual host coordinates with api.hostX() , hostY() and hostZ() ; use api.playerX() and its counterparts for the player.

title: Managing instances
text: Reload a saved program through the program list. Reload first if a revision conflict occurs. In the instance list, select a UUID to inspect diagnostics or revoke it to stop execution. A real handover preserves item state; a copy receives its own identity and fresh data. Player variables remain separate by player UUID. The limits are 128 programs and 2,048 issued instances. Source, data, timers and execution/effect quotas follow the shared script limits . Every binding creates a new instance, so do not bind again just to transfer an item between players.

title: Shops, mail and companions
text: Configure shops, banks and teleporters. Send mail with attachments and hire NPC companions.

title: Trader: your first offer
text: Open the shop settings in the NPC editor and enable the shop. Add an offer. For example, use minecraft:emerald as currency, price 1 , minecraft:bread as goods and goods amount 3 . Enable the offer and Allow buying . Buying is from the player's perspective: the player pays currency and receives goods. To allow selling back, enable Allow selling . The player hands over the configured quantity of goods and receives currency. This uses the same item pair and base price. Save the shop. Try Shift + right-click → Shop with the required currency and room in your inventory. A shop supports up to 16 offers. Items use registry IDs, so you can also use items from installed mods. An enabled shop needs at least one usable offer before players can open it. Buying and selling have separate toggles, reputation requirements and limits. Also check whom the configured limit applies to. Reputation and event tabs let you configure discounts and temporary discount events. If a trade fails, check currency, quantities, inventory space, reputation and exhausted limits. Correct invalid item IDs before saving.

title: Banker
text: Select the Banker primary role in the editor, set the bank title and a size of 1–6 rows of nine slots, then save. Players open the bank from the NPC's service menu and move items like in a container. A vault belongs to one player at one particular NPC. Players do not see each other's items, and a different NPC has a separate vault. A cloned banker is therefore not another access point to the original bank. Before changing capacity or removing a banker, arrange for stored contents to be handled and back up the world.

title: Teleporter
text: Select the Teleporter primary role. Set an existing dimension, such as minecraft:overworld , the destination coordinates and viewing direction. For a free teleport, leave the cost item ID blank and the amount at 0. For a paid teleport, set a valid item and quantity, such as 2 × minecraft:emerald . Save and try Use teleporter from the service menu. Prepare clear, safe space with a floor at the destination coordinates. Checking the dimension and world bounds is not a search for a safe landing area. The cost is removed after a successful teleport; invalid coordinates, an invalid price or insufficient items produce a message.

title: Mail between players
text: Open your mailbox with /ardanpcs_mail . Alternatively, enable the additional postman service in an NPC's editor and select Mail from its services. Enabling mail does not replace dialogue or other roles. Start a new letter in the mailbox and search for a recipient by name or UUID. Enter the subject and message. The recipient must already be known to the server by having joined it. They can receive mail while offline. Optionally select attachments and quantities from your current inventory. Do not move selected items before sending. Send the letter and check Sent . The recipient opens Inbox , reads the message and claims its attachments. The subject allows up to 80 characters and the message 2,000. A letter supports up to four attachment slots, with at most 64 items per slot. Item components such as custom names, enchantments and damage are preserved. An ordinary player can send three letters per minute. The inventory must fit all attachments at once. If space is insufficient, nothing is claimed; free some room and try again. The mailbox supports read status and replies. Deleting unclaimed attachments requires confirmation that they will be discarded permanently. Hiding a sent copy does not destroy the recipient's attachments. For a story message from an NPC, use the api.mail script operation . It sends text without attachments to the current player and uses a unique delivery key to prevent repeated delivery.

title: Hireable companions
text: Enable the additional companion service in the NPC editor. Set the hire price, duration of 60–604800 real seconds, default mode, optional safe catch-up teleport and an owner limit of 1–3. A price of 0 makes hiring free. A player can have at most three hires in total, including suspended payments. The player chooses Shift + right-click → Companion , reads the price and duration, then hires the NPC. At the same NPC they can change its mode or dismiss it. Controls are available to the owner nearby in the same dimension. Changes to the configured price or duration affect future contracts. Mode Behaviour Follow Follows the owner without choosing attack targets. Wait Stops movement and attacks; swimming remains possible. Defend Follows and reacts to a recent attacker of the owner or NPC, or a recent target of the owner. Hire time continues while the player is offline and while the server is stopped. An offline owner's companion waits. When the owner dies, it switches to Wait; the owner must change the mode again after respawning. It does not travel between dimensions after its owner, instead returning home in its own dimension. Catch-up teleport works only within the same dimension, into loaded chunks and when a suitable location is found. Otherwise normal navigation remains. A companion does not force chunks to load and cannot simultaneously act as a quest escort. Defence respects friendly relationships, teams, factions, server PvP and the attack-players setting. After expiry or confirmed dismissal, the NPC returns home and the hire ends. The price is not refunded. Cloning an NPC copies service configuration, not the owner or an active contract.

title: When a payment or attachment is suspended
text: After an uncertain save, mail or a paid hire may require administrator recovery. Do not repeatedly add or remove items by hand without checking. The administrator first compares the actual inventory with the records; confirming recovery does not create items or refund a price by itself. Mail: the Recovery required tab for OP2. /ardanpcs_companion list [page] : list suspended contracts. /ardanpcs_companion recovery <NPC UUID> : repair a contract even if its NPC is missing. /ardanpcs_transfer pending : list unresolved shared transfers. Handle recovery with the affected player online and a world backup. Administrator guidance continues in troubleshooting .

title: Troubleshooting and backups
text: Check permissions, saving, appearance and script diagnostics, and learn where world data lives before updating or restoring a backup.

title: Start with these checks
text: Check Minecraft 1.21.8 , Java 21 or newer , Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer , and Fabric API 0.136.1+1.21.8 or a compatible newer build for 1.21.8. Use the same ArdaNPCs version on the server and every client. Keep only one version of its JAR in mods/ . Check that you are launching the intended profile and world. NPC data belongs to a specific world. Read the in-game error and the relevant part of logs/latest.log on both server and client. Problem Next step The editor will not open or save Permissions and saving A skin, cape or model is missing Appearance and models A script does nothing or has been disabled Script diagnostics Data is missing after restart or cannot load Data storage and world backups

title: Editor access and permissions
text: NPC administration, appearance editing and script editing require operator permission level 2 or higher. Creative mode alone does not provide these permissions. If a command is missing or denied, ask the server administrator to check your account's permissions. Run /ardanpcs manager in-game as an authorised player. The manager is a client GUI and cannot open in the server console. If the command reports a missing client mod, check that ArdaNPCs and Fabric API are installed in your game profile too. After changing the version or modpack, reconnect with the correct set of mods.

title: A change was not saved or disappeared after restart
text: Complete the relevant save action: Save appearance for skins and capes, the script panel's Save for scripts, or apply the model selection and then save the main editor. Read the confirmation or error. A preview or an edited field does not confirm a disk write. If two editors conflict, review your draft against the current state before saving again. For a write failure, check free disk space, the server process's file permissions and file locks. In the server log, look for the exact path and messages such as Failed to write or Cannot safely load . NPC definitions live at <world>/data/ardanpcs/npcs.json . A different world or server instance uses a different NPC collection. This file alone does not contain every quest, player or inventory record. The storage system uses .bak files. If a primary JSON is damaged, it tries a valid backup and preserves the damaged bytes in a .corrupt-* file. If neither primary nor backup is valid, loading fails instead of replacing the data with an empty collection. Do not delete damaged stores or replace them with empty JSON to clear an error. Stop the server, preserve a copy of the entire world and log, then restore a verified backup. Make manual data repairs while the server is stopped. Reload is not a backup or an undo command.

title: A skin, cape or model is missing
text: Player skin or PNG Skins and capes apply to the humanoid body. A selected mob model uses that mob's renderer. For a player profile, use Look up player followed by Save appearance . Check the name/UUID; retry later if the official service is unavailable. For imports, check the server's config/arda_npcs/import_textures/ folder, actual PNG format and maximum size of 256 KiB. Skins must be 64 × 64 or 64 × 32 pixels; capes must be 64 × 32. If a file is missing from the picker, try a simple name such as guard.png and refresh the list. Do not use subdirectories or directory links. The list shows at most 64 files. If the import quota is full, do not delete random world assets: other NPCs, templates or corpses may reference them. The world limit is 1024 assets and 64 MiB of content. Plan further changes using a backup and an inventory of textures in use. For resource packs, check the identifier and that clients have the same texture. For URLs, check a direct, reachable PNG address; capes require HTTPS. For the setup and import procedure, see Appearance, skins and models . An entity model reverted to a humanoid Check the full entity ID and that its mod is installed on both server and client. Select the model again, apply the selection and save the main editor. Check the client log for a model creation or rendering failure. ArdaNPCs uses its default appearance after such a failure. Try another entity from the same mod. Its custom renderer may need state the helper model does not supply. After resolving the cause, restart the client and try the model again; failed types are remembered during the client session. A missing special animation does not necessarily mean the model failed to save. The NPC does not inherit the other entity's AI or abilities, and universal GeckoLib compatibility is not guaranteed. A larger hitbox does not teach an NPC to fly or use the original mob's attacks.

title: A script does nothing or has been disabled
text: Open the NPC's Scripts panel. Check that scripting is enabled and that the intended event contains code. Enter the event body, not a wrapper event function copied from another mod. Run Check . Fix reported syntax problems or unsupported API calls. Run Test for the chosen event. This is a simulation, not an actual reward grant or world change. Click Output and read the Diagnostics and result panel. It shows the last error and a limited api.log history. Save after fixing the script. A successful save clears the stored failure block and allows execution to resume. ArdaNPCs uses its own restricted server-side JavaScript API. CustomNPCs scripts are not drop-in compatible. Review and fix unsupported operations reported by the importer; conversion does not prove a script works in every modpack. For a shared execution budget warning, reduce frequent events, lengthy loops and effects. Do not use tight retry loops instead of timers. A predicate is read-only and must not change the world or stored variables. If diagnostics report Script runtime unavailable: storage could not be loaded safely , resolve the data-loading problem and inspect the server log first. Script runtime state is stored at <world>/data/ardanpcs/scripts-state.json ; do not clear it as the first troubleshooting step.

title: Back up and update
text: Exit the game or stop the server normally, and wait for saving to finish. Copy the entire world. Include vanilla player data, mod data and data/ardanpcs/appearance-assets/ . Keep the active configuration, mod versions and any custom resource packs as well. Source PNGs for future imports live outside the world in config/arda_npcs/import_textures/ . Try the new version on a separate copy of the world first. Update ArdaNPCs on server and clients and remove the old JAR from the active mods/ directory. Check the editor, a dialogue/quest, saving across a restart, appearance on a second client and the services you actually use. npcs.json alone is not a complete server backup. Templates live at <world>/data/ardanpcs/templates.json , and imported images have separate files. Moving only the JSON to a different world does not move those images. To return to an older version, restore the matching complete world backup and mod set. Replacing the JAR alone does not undo changes to saved data. Individual .bak files help recover stores but do not replace a full world backup.

title: What to include in a bug report
text: Minecraft, ArdaNPCs, Fabric Loader and Fabric API versions, and whether you are playing singleplayer or on a server. Short steps from opening the editor to the failure, plus the expected result. For a model problem, the exact entity ID and the supplying mod's name and version. For a script problem, the event, a short relevant code sample and the diagnostic message. The relevant client or server log section from the time of the problem. Remove private details and login information before posting it.
